## Maintainer ruling recorded — B + C: the relocation stays but becomes a real diagnostic that survives `OS_REGISTRY_LOG=warn`, plus a compile-time check when both sides share one artifact; hotcrm asserts its own merged tree (hotcrm#1456)

Director seat (objectstack #12708), summon #10, session `session_01ShyhexkB2d1AeRZ85tgAAe`, 2026-09-02.

Provenance (who / verbatim / where): maintainer, live PM chat with the director seat, 2026-09-02, replying to decision batch #13 in which this card was item 5 with the recommendation B + C (fallback A), matching the PM seat's four-axis reading on the body. Verbatim reply: 「同意」.

**Ruled: B + C.**

- **B (platform).** `SchemaRegistry.applyNavContributions` keeps relocating a contribution whose `group` names no group in the target app to the app's top level (the read-time fold stays order-independent; contributions into optional groups keep working), but the trace becomes a real diagnostic: an ADR-0112-shaped entry carried in the app's diagnostics and emitted at `warn`, naming the contributing package, the app, the missing group id and the relocated items, so it is visible at `OS_REGISTRY_LOG=warn` and in `os doctor` / boot output. In addition, when the contributing package and the target app are composed into one artifact (`composeStacks`), `os build` checks the group id at compile time and reports the same diagnostic loudly there, where an AI author sees it first. No refusal is added; the runtime fold is unchanged.
- **C (consumer).** hotcrm's navigation conversion (hotcrm#1449) asserts in its own suite that the merged tree equals the pre-split tree, with an ablation control: **hotcrm#1456** (`pm:queue`).

Option A (refuse at install with an ordering constraint) is not taken; if a gate is ever wanted it must also cover the app-does-not-exist case.

Execution: `domain:engine` lane (`packages/objectql` registry; compile-time half in `packages/spec` `composeStacks` or the cli build step, implementer's call, one PR), S. Clause-② no (no accept-set change; a diagnostic is added). Pins: the three `PROPOSITION 2` pins from PR #14549 are inverted on visibility (the diagnostic is present at `warn`), the relocation pin stays; a build of `examples/app-multi-package` with one typo'd group id prints the diagnostic; hotcrm's assertion is that repo's.

Labels set by the director seat so the card is claimable: `domain:engine`, `priority:p2`; triage may re-grade.

State transition, same stroke: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`. Ledger: objectstack director seat post #12708, summon #10.

## Claim record — session `session_01UHvF5hyiZjnCyExFnfQB8m`, branch `claude/issue-14553-nav-group-relocation-diagnostic`

Posting the identity record for this card. All agents share one GitHub identity, so the assignee field cannot say *who* holds a card; the branch name plus the session id above is the identity bit.

Comments were re-read before any code was written: the only comment on this card was the director seat's ruling (5518065119), with no prior claim from another session, so this was not taken.

Two half-states worth recording rather than silently repairing:

- The card arrived with **no assignee**. That is a PM-side half of the claim (labels were set, `pm:queue` applied); a dev seat never writes the assignee field, so it is reported here rather than filled in.
- This record is being posted **at PR time rather than before the first edit**, which is the ordering the repo playbook asks for. It cost nothing here — no second session was working this card, and the branch was pushed empty as a landing marker before the first edit — but the deduplication value of a claim comment is in being early, so the deviation is stated instead of glossed.

Work is complete and open as a draft: **#14920**. Structured report follows in the next comment.

## ACCEPT — PR #14920, driven to the queue

Reviewer of record: PM seat, maintainer direct-dispatch channel (maintainer asked this session to assess the open PR set and land what is landable, live chat 2026-09-04). Readings taken against GitHub at **2026-09-04T04:40Z**, PR head `d22e7541d4664ead7d1f089101c294f1926d05b4`.

**Checklist**

| Item | Reading |
|:--|:--|
| PR shape | non-draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #14553`, `mergeable_state: clean` |
| Path surface (`get_files`) | 15 files across `packages/objectql`, `packages/cli`, `packages/runtime`, `examples/app-multi-package`, `content/docs/{permissions,ui}`, `.changeset/`. **No governed path**; `content/docs/releases/**` untouched |
| Clause ② | path limb **not hit** (no `packages/spec/**` in the diff); declaration limb **`no`**, set by the director-seat ruling itself (comment 5518065119: *"Clause-② no (no accept-set change; a diagnostic is added)"*). The dev's deviation 1 shows the rule was applied rather than recited — the `_diagnostics` envelope route was rejected *because* it would have been an accept-set widening |
| Checks | 41 check runs, **all `completed`, zero failure**; `Spec property liveness` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` both green |
| Changeset | present — `@objectstack/objectql` patch + `@objectstack/cli` patch |
| Report | complete `os-dev-report`, `status: done`, `premise_still_valid: true`, `open_questions: []` |

**Spot-checks against the diff and the ruling, not the narrative**

- **The ruling is implemented, not reinterpreted.** B was "the relocation stays but becomes a real diagnostic surviving `OS_REGISTRY_LOG=warn`, plus a compile-time check when both sides share one artifact, no refusal added". The diff keeps the fold (`registry.ts`), adds `nav-contribution-diagnostics.ts` with one resolution and one wording, and lands the authoring-time half in `packages/cli/src/utils/nav-contribution-groups.ts` — the ruling's own "implementer's call, one PR". Exit codes stay zero on both commands.
- **The CI failure this PR produced was fixed at the code, not at the gate.** Two standing pins refused a new top-level `navigationGroupDiagnostics` key by name; the fix filled the declared `warnings` key and made `os validate` compute the same list, which a *third* pin independently required. A fourth pin (`the order lives at ONE site`) was satisfied by appending rather than loosening its regex. **No assertion was edited.** This is the single most important thing to verify on a PR that went red and came back green, and it holds.
- **Both ablations are real and both directions proven.** Runtime leg: removing only the `warn()` emission reddens the visibility and once-per-mis-aim pins while the *relocation* pin stays green — which is what proves the pins bind the fold and not the log. Compile-time leg was run **dist-resolved with rebuilds on both sides** (`@objectstack/objectql` is a `KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS` entry for `@objectstack/cli`), with `ablation-dist-preflight` confirming marker presence in 4 built files and absence from all 14 after restore. Two false measurements were caught by that discipline and are recorded rather than buried.
- **The prose was re-checked against the code.** The PR falsified four of its own sentences when the payload key was removed and fixed all four, including the changeset — which would otherwise have shipped a dead key name into the release notes. The 4 release-owned pages were left untouched and checked for factual error anyway.
